newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas gains despite milder weather ahead.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas gains despite milder weather ahead.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly higher Friday, except in the Northeast market areas where temperatures were expected to return to more normal levels this weekend, industry sources said.

At the New York city-gate, prices slumped into the $3.30s and $3.40s, as compared to Thursday's high of about $3.80, ladened by milder weather forecast for the region this weekend and into the early part of next week.
Gulf Coast gas traded about four to five cents higher into the mid-$2.70s to about $2.80, with the higher-priced deals confirmed done shortly before nomination deadlines.

In the New York market, gas inventories are near full, as reported by the American Gas Association, so utilities may be opting to take from storage, thereby causing prices to soften significantly, traders speculated.
However, because gas stocks are only about 73 percent full in the producing region, traders said, buyers are reluctant to withdraw and instead are entering the spot market to meet heating demand.
As a result, prices on the Midcontinent pipes gained about three to five cents to the mid-$2.50s to low-$2.60s, with Chicago city-gate quoted around $3.10.
Similarly in south Texas, prices rose by about two cents to the low-$2.60s despite the mild weather now in the state.
In west Texas, Permian prices edged up about one to two cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s, supported by storage withdrawals and a strong demand in the West.
At the southern California border, gas sold in the high-$2.60s to about $2.70 as West Coast utilities continued to demand large volumes of Canadian gas.
